page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m4.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance deployed on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 Intel Xeon processor running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz, configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores utilizing hyper-threading. The processor architecture includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of shared L3 cache, with support for instruction set extensions including AVX-512 and AES. Memory capacity totals 16.0 GB, maintaining an even 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not feature bundled local storage or discrete GPU acceleration, relying on external network-attached volumes, and provides a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate compute and throughput performance situated predominantly in the lower tier relative to broader cloud hardware. The system recorded a Geekbench single-core score of 1045.0 and a multi-core score of 2281.0, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 4175.8. Memory bandwidth reaches 25.28 GB/s on large uncached reads and 22.66 GB/s on uncached writes, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and image processing benchmarks placed in the lowest tenth percentile. In network and application evaluations, the instance supported 3.35 million Redis SET operations per second and 3.29 GB/s in static web serving throughput. For small language model inference, it processed prompt tokens at 247.89 tokens per second on a 135M model.

From an infrastructure cost perspective, the instance provides an economical entry point for applications requiring dedicated vCPUs and moderate memory without the expense of high-frequency compute or integrated NVMe storage tiers. The trade-off is reflected in restrained compute and I/O performance scores, making it suboptimal for latency-sensitive or high-concurrency database workloads. The ecs.u1-c1m4.xlarge is primarily suited for general utility workloads, including low-traffic web serving, microservices, continuous integration runners, lightweight caching nodes, and development environments.

Powered by an Intel Xeon processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, it supplies 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, accompanied by a 33 MB L3 cache and AVX-512 instruction support. The instance includes 16.0 GB of memory, reflecting a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory distribution, alongside a 2 Gbps baseline network connection. It does not bundle local disk storage or discrete GPUs. In synthetic benchmarks, the instance consistently scores in the lower quartile, registering a Geekbench single-core score of 1045.0, a multi-core score of 2281.0, and 3.35 million Redis SET operations per second. With its balanced resource ratio and lower compute intensity, the instance serves as a cost-effective allocation for basic web servers, staging environments, light microservices, and secondary background tasks.
